_comment: The BASELINE every scenario diffs from: a signed-in wallet that holds
nothing. Empty is the default, but every body here is the shape the wire
contract actually specifies - an 'empty' body of the wrong shape is worse
than no fixture at all, because the screen renders its ERROR view and a
careless test reads that as 'empty'.
Every entry names the type it is bound to. Change one only against
packages/mallow_api/openapi/openapi.yaml or the hand-written model, never
against what a screen appears to accept.
Endpoints deliberately LEFT to the generic DEFAULT, with reasons - do not
add them without one:
* POST /v0/authToken - the signed-login step-up. Answering it would send
the app on to signLoginChallenge + /v0/authToken/verify, i.e. a real
signature and a Set-Cookie the mock cannot produce, so a 'helpful'
fixture would start a flow no case is written for.
* GET /home - the home feed. `{ "result": {} }` IS the correct empty
body (ApiResponse<HomeFeedResponse>; every inner field defaults), and
it was tried: serving it makes `HomeBloc._revalidate` succeed, which
runs `HomeFeedRepository.cacheAllHomeSections` -> an INSERT into
cached_home_feed. That write is issued from a bloc handler that
outlives the test - five section fetches are awaited first - so when
`restartApp` closes the drift connection under it, drift throws
'Tried to send Request ... but the connection was closed!' into the
zone, and the framework pins it on whichever case is running by then.
Measured: 2 such aborts in one config-and-network run. That is an app
bug (an unguarded cache write after teardown,
home_feed_repository.dart:158) and it has to be fixed before the feed
can be fixtured; the home-feed bucket is Phase 2 and owns both.
* GET /v2/health - not the app. It is the readiness probe
test/e2e/lib.sh uses to decide the mock is up.
* POST /v0/userWithDetails, GET /v0/txFees, POST /v1/bugReport - only
reached by the listing / mint / bug-report flows, which are Phase 2-3.
Their bodies belong with those fixtures, where a case can assert on
them.

routes._note: Non-JSON-RPC POST to the proxy root. RPC verbs never match this (they need `rpc`); they fall through to the built-ins.

Helius DAS searchAssets, the Solana token+NFT read. NOT a built-in verb, so without this it answers `result: null` - which TokenRepository degrades to zero tokens WITHOUT erroring. That silent false-empty is the trap this route exists to close: the tab looks empty because the mock said nothing, not because the wallet holds nothing. Body is a real empty-portfolio response.
`{ result: [EvmHolding, ...] }` per getV2EvmBalances; /v2/tezos/balances reuses it. Reading anything but `result` yields `?? const []`, i.e. a silent zero-holdings answer.
PortfolioArtworksResponse (in openapi.yaml): `result` + `total` both REQUIRED. A missing `total` throws inside the generated fromJson and the Portfolio tab shows its error view.
PortfolioGroupsResponse (in openapi.yaml) wrapping PortfolioGroupsResult: `groups` + `total` both REQUIRED.
ActivityListResponse (packages/mallow_api .../models/activity.dart): `result` + `pagination` both required, and ActivityPagination requires page/limit/hasMore.
BulkUserLookupResponse: `result` is required (its two lists default). Requested on every session init and every drawer open.
NotificationUnreadCountResponse -> NotificationUnreadCount: both fields required. Drives the drawer's unread badge.
EvmTokenListResponse under a `result` envelope: version/updatedAt/tokens all required. An empty list is the correct sandbox answer - no ERC-20 is verified here.
ApiResponse<TokenPricesResponse>: a mint->price map, empty here.
The remote-config kill switch. Nothing killed, no forced update.

Jupiter price v3. THE reason the suite was not offline: TokenRepository reaches _fetchSolPrice() on the balances path whenever no native price is supplied, so a contributor's run sent real traffic to api.jup.ag from their own IP. v3 answers a FLAT map, mint -> price object, with no `data` envelope, and omits any mint it has no price for -- so an empty map is the valid 'nothing is priced' answer rather than an error.

CoinGecko, reached through GeckoTerminalService for charts and pool reads. One regex for the whole /api/v3 surface: the suite asserts no chart data, so the point is that the call is answered locally rather than leaving the machine.

IPFS and Arweave gateways. Media is never asserted in the suite, so these answer an empty object rather than bytes -- the image fails to decode, which is what an unreachable gateway already looked like. The containment is the point: without these two the app walks to ipfs.io and arweave.net for real.
